doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

chapter: Vegas, clubs and the jazz life
title: Playing for love of the music
summary: Great choruses lost at late-night sessions; they learned to play for love, not a living.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: disappeared into air, at sessions at three o’clock in the morning in Harlem and at the jazzkellers in Germany or little roadside cafes where somebody felt like playing and took out the horn and went up and played with the rhythm section you know, on a Sunday afternoon. There used to be places in Buffalo where, I mean all over the world there were places where you could go and play and you could practice. Now you’d practice, but you’d go out and show your wares.
And it was for the love of it. We learned to play for the love of it, not because we thought we were going to make a living on it.
